description: Claude Code ignores `hooks` in a plugin-shipped agent's frontmatter, so the plugin's two agents are gated here. (1) SubagentStop gates the designtwin:screen-builder subagent with the same plan check build-screen runs. The script reads the hook JSON from stdin (only when stdin is not a terminal, never waiting on a silent pipe), exits immediately when design/plan/ has no open plan, checks only the plans the subagent's own tool calls wrote (Write/Edit, or the plan-skeleton call's --out in a Bash or PowerShell command; other shell commands are not read) and the plan that alone lists a file it wrote with Write/Edit — nothing when it claimed none, e.g. it edited only files several plans share, and then it blocks once (decision block; the reason, which Claude Code delivers to the subagent as its next instruction, names the open plans and has the builder run verify-build <plan.json> on the plan it built and name that plan in its report, or say it built none — a SubagentStop systemMessage was observed not to be displayed by Claude Code 2.1.299, so the builder is told instead), and its next stop (stop_hook_active) passes unchecked, so it never loops; every open plan when the payload carries no readable agent transcript — on a checked plan it blocks only on an unexplained colour literal, an unanchored visible design node or (web profiles) no data-dt-node tag at all, never writes plan.status, and stops itself at 60 s — the timeout below is the harness's backstop. (2) PreToolUse guards the designtwin:visual-verifier subagent's Bash, PowerShell and Write calls (the payload's agent_type; a call from anyone else gets no answer, so the normal permission flow applies): it refuses a write outside design/verify/ and the run cache node_modules/.cache/designtwin-verify/ (or to a tool-owned file there), a pattern kill (pkill, killall, …), a dependency or Playwright browser install, and dangerouslyDisableSandbox (a PowerShell call is judged like a Bash one — its quoting, Stop-Process -Name / Get-Process … | Stop-Process as pattern kills; as for Bash, the files a command writes are not read) — a deny decision with the reason on stdout, exit 0; a payload it cannot read is allowed and logged to stderr.
